title: Turn a topic into a narrated explainer video with sources
summary: A developer built a Claude Code skill that researches a topic, writes a sourced script, adds voiceover and renders a 1080p explainer video, with sample films published.
agent_role: The agent picks an angle, compiles a fact list with sources, writes and self-reviews narration, generates voice, codes and renders the video, and checks it. The human approves the topic, the script and storyboard, any paid image generation, and the final cut.
outcome: The author shares several finished sample videos of 1 to 3 minutes; one enhanced episode used 246 credits of paid image and video generation.
what_they_did: A developer packaged a Claude Code skill in Chinese with 44 visual styles. You give it a topic, and it builds a fact list with a source for every number and quote. It writes narration, has a helper agent critique it, records an AI voice, then draws and renders each frame in code. It stops three times for your approval.
how_it_went: The repo shows sample videos on topics like ancient food storage and how rockets fly. The basic version costs no generation credits; the enhanced one used 246 credits for one episode, the author says.
worth_knowing: The free tier draws everything in code; paid AI images are only used for a few key shots, priced up front, and labeled as AI illustrations in the video.
prompt: Make a short explainer video about [your topic] in [language]. First propose an angle, a target length and a visual style, and wait for my approval. Then build a fact list where every number, name, date and quote has a source, noting where sources disagree. Write the narration and a shot list, and show them to me before producing anything. After I approve, record narration with [voice tool], build the animation in code, render at 1080p, and check the on-screen text against the fact list. Ask before using any paid image or video generation, and show the estimated cost.

curation.rationale: A detailed, open-source workflow where Claude Code researches, scripts, voices and renders sourced explainer videos, with sample videos and approval checkpoints; strong non-coding creative/education use.
